messages:
maya (eng-security): FYI — audit flagged a short-lived binding where a svcacct from org-alpha could list projects in org-beta :thinking_face:
ops-bot: [ALERT] policy-evaluator: binding-slip detected: member=serviceAccount:sa-cross@org-alpha role=project.viewer target=org-beta/project-42 timestamp=2026-03-20T09:12:03Z
sahil (eng-plat): ugh. reproducer or logs?
maya (eng-security): saw it in the policy-eval logs and stackdriver trace. attaching snippet:
```
policy_eval: evaluateBinding(binding_id=bbf7c)
matched_member: serviceAccount:sa-cross@org-alpha
matched_target: org-beta/project-42
decision: ALLOW (via fallback-route)
```
eli (infra): fallback-route? that sounds like the routing policy that maps legacy aliases during a migration. could be a race with the alias normalization job.
jordan (privacy): can we assume data exfil risk? did any secrets get read?
maya (eng-security): initial access logs show only GET on /v1/projects/42/config (read-only). no secret reads in the 60s window. still want full audit export.
sahil (eng-plat): quick mitigation: revoke the specific binding and block the alias mapping path. run:
```
gcloud projects remove-iam-policy-binding 42 --member="serviceAccount:sa-cross@org-alpha" --role="roles/viewer"
```
eli (infra): running revoke now. also rotating service account key for sa-cross and disabling token minting for 5m.
ops-bot: [ACTION] revoke-iam 42 sa-cross@org-alpha requested by eli — started
maya (eng-security): thanks. can someone dump the policy-evaluator version and config? we might have regressed after the alias-refactor.
sahil (eng-plat): policy-evaluator v2.8.1 on prod. config: `enable_alias_fallback=true` with a 250ms cache TTL. suspect stale cache + concurrent churn.
eli (infra): I see a spike in config-update events at 09:11:52, several alias rewrites. race window ~ 09:11:52-09:12:05.
jordan (privacy): I'll open a retention slice and export all access logs for project-42 and sa-cross for that time range. need legal/incident notice?
maya (eng-security): low-likelihood PII touch but escalate to sec+privacy as precaution. jordan, can you confirm by EOD?
ops-bot: [AUDIT] policy-eval-trace bbf7c appended to incident-3452
sahil (eng-plat): short-term fix: disable alias fallback until we patch the TTL bug. patch plan: make fallback consult authoritative mapping store first, then cache result, avoid allowing non-canonical member matches.
eli (infra): deploying a feature-flag rollback to turn off `enable_alias_fallback` in prod across 4 regions. ETA 4m.
maya (eng-security): good. also add a targeted alert: if a member from org-A is granted to any resource owned by org-B then escalate to pager.
jordan (privacy): export done, pushing to secure bucket s3://redwood-priv-exfil/incident-3452/ — permissioned to sec+privacy only.
maya (eng-security): confirmed revoke completed and fallback flag off. can someone validate no other bindings were affected by the same code path?
sahil (eng-plat): running global scan for alias-derived bindings: `scripts/find_alias_bindings --since 2026-03-20T08:00` — returns 3 hits, two were benign (test orgs), one is this incident.
eli (infra): rolling forward a small fix to policy-evaluator to require tenant-id canonicalization before allowing cross-tenant matches. deploy in 12m with canary.
maya (eng-security): assigning follow-ups: sahil to PR fix + tests, eli to rollback/monitoring changes, jordan to final audit export + privacy memo. cc @oncall
jordan (privacy): will draft memo and send to legal by EOD.
maya (eng-security): final note — we need a postmortem template entry for "alias normalization race leading to temporary cross-tenant allow". I'll start the doc and include timeline + mitigations.
ops-bot: [DEPLOY] feature-flag rollback performed in us-east1/us-west1/eu-west1 — ok
maya (eng-security): thanks everyone. keeping this thread open for notes until the postmortem is ready.
